newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Pol Pot taken, Khmer Rouge said finished.
newsitem.headline: Pol Pot taken, Khmer Rouge said finished.

text.p: Khmer Rouge strongman Pol Pot, whose "killing fields" rule in the 1970s devastated Cambodia, has been captured and efforts will be made to try him before an international court, the Cambodian government said on Saturday.

First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh and his uneasy coalition partner and co-premier, Hun Sen, said the hated communist guerrilla leader and one of right-hand men had been caught by former comrades who turned against the hard-line communist veteran.
"This is the end of the Khmer Rouge," Hun Sen told reporters.
"Prince Ranariddh and I agree that this is a gift to the Cambodian people," he said.
Hun Sen said Pol Pot and Khieu Samphan, the guerrilla group's nominal leader, were caught by a Khmer Rouge splinter faction which broke away earlier this month.
"Before the lower ranks said they had broken away but now they've arrested Pol Pot ... It's over," Hun Sen said.

The two prime ministers were speaking after emerging from talks with visiting Thai prime minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh. It was the first time in recent weeks the two leaders presented a unified front on the Khmer Rouge.
Prince Ranariddh said the Khmer Rouge guerrilla army was now finished both politically and militarily.

He said Pol Pot should be sent to an international tribunal to answer for the excesses of his 1975-79 "killing fields" regime when the radical guerrilla group's name became synonymous with starvation, vicious torture and mass execution.

"We agree with each other that Pol Pot will be brought ... eventually to Phnom Penh and the two prime ministers are going to send a letter to the United Nations secretary general to ask him to set up an international tribunal to try Pol Pot," the prince said.

Khmer Rouge radio, which is under the control of the breakaway faction, announced on Friday in a broadcast from the north Cambodian jungle guerrilla zone, that its army captured the 69-yeaar-old Pol Pot the previous day.

The two premiers did not elaborate on the precise whereabouts of Pol Pot and Khieu Samphan, nor when they might be brought to Phnom Penh. There was no information about the fate of other key Khmer Rouge leaders either.
The breakaway Khmer Rouge faction which captured Pol Pot would be integrated into government forces after formally surrendering, they said.

Ranariddh said on Friday that forces from the splinter group were closing in on Pol Pot who was holed up in a land-mine strewn mountain camp in northern Cambodia, guarded by his last band of loyal fighters.

Pol Pot, whose Khmer Rouge government was responsible for the death of more than a million Cambodians, has not been seen in public since 1980 two years after his overthrow at the hands of an invading Vietnamese army.
He was sentenced to death in absentia by a Phnom Penh court soon after his overthrow.

The Khmer Rouge waged a low-intensity guerrilla war against the government after boycotting a 1993 election supervised by the United Nations but the once-formidable Maoist guerrilla army was decimated in recent years by government offensives, splits and defections.
The hated Pol Pot led the die-hard rump of the Khmer Rouge from its northern stronghold of Anlong Veng until earlier this month when bitter factional violence erupted.
Pol Pot fled from Anlong Veng after ordering the slaughter of his defence chief Son Sen and almost a dozen members of his family. REUTER sc kr rsb
